To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of channel coupling on charge symmetry breaking (CSB) in the np system are significant and become increasingly important above 500 MeV lab energy.
the effects of mass splittings on charge symmetry breaking are significant at about 500MeV laboratory energy and are not significant for lower energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of charge symmetry breaking effects in the neutron-proton system.
the charge symmetry breaking in nucleon-nucleon scattering.
the study of charge symmetry breaking in neutron proton elastic scattering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
charge symmetry breaking effects in np scattering are not large at low energies and are not well understood at high energies.
charge symmetry breaking in np elastic scattering is not a good probe of the charge symmetry of the strong interaction.
the charge symmetry breaking effects in np scattering above pion threshold are small and are not well established by the present experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
charge symmetry is broken by about 0.5% in np elastic scattering at 400 MeV and by about 1% at 500 MeV.
charge symmetry breaking is not a good observable to use to probe the effects of the N.6. channel.
charge symmetry breaking in elastic np scattering above the pion production threshold is not a very significant effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
charge symmetry breaking in np scattering is a sensitive probe of the mass splitting in the nucleon and the delta multiplets.
the charge symmetry violation (CSV) in the np elastic scattering cross section is not a reliable indicator of the strength of CSV in the N.6. channel.
the effect of the N.6. channel on the charge asymmetry is not as dramatic as has been previously suggested.
